setup: Just a reminder to check on your elderly relatives during these hot summer months.
punchline: Hi Dad. There, my job’s done.

setup: A Baltimore Raven published a complex study in a math journal.
punchline: The NFL suspended him for unsportsmanlike conduct.

setup: I lost $500 betting yesterday.
punchline: Not on the Super Bowl, on “Downton Abbey.”

setup: It's being reported that Google and Yahoo are in serious talks to buy Hulu.
punchline: I don't have a joke here, I just wanted to confuse my mother.

setup: Last night I was visited by a ghost who claimed he had "unfinished business."
punchline: Turns out he just needed something notarized.

setup: ABC announced that the "The Bachelor" and "The Bachelorette" will now feature a more diverse cast.
punchline: They’re going to add a contestant who has read a book.

setup: A college student in Georgia was worried that his parents would be mad at him for flunking English, so he faked his own kidnapping.
punchline: However, the parents figured it out when the ransom note said, "We Has Your Son."

setup: A new report says that 80% of sunscreens either don't work or have questionable ingredients.
punchline: In a related story, I don’t have long to live.

setup: Yesterday, a woman gave birth after running the Chicago Marathon.
punchline: Immediately after the race, the baby was disqualified for cheating.

setup: While working on the LA subway, construction workers have discovered fossils from the ice age.
punchline: The fossils belong to the last creature to ever use the Los Angeles subway.

setup: An Ohio school is requiring students who want to be on the yearbook committee be tested for drugs.
punchline: The yearbook committee is protesting, saying, "If we were cool enough to do drugs, we wouldn't be on the yearbook committee."

setup: This weekend was the first YouTube Music Awards show and Eminem won Artist of the Year.
punchline: Second runner up was a cat walking across a piano.

setup: Sunday was daylight savings time, when we lose an hour for no apparent reason.
punchline: And, by the way, "losing an hour for no apparent reason" is also the motto for this show.

setup: Bono has apologized for putting the U2 album in peoples' iTunes without their permission.
punchline: For the full version of his apology, check your voicemail, it’s there.

setup: This holiday weekend, Chicago's Midway airport is featuring live blues and jazz performances for passengers waiting at baggage claim.
punchline: Not to be outdone, New York's JFK airport will feature baggage belonging to the passengers in Chicago.

setup: There’s a cold snap, and even in Hollywood, temperatures are in the 50s.
punchline: Of course, since it’s Hollywood, the weather is telling everyone it’s only in its mid-30s.

setup: It’s rumored that the new PlayStation controller will measure the degree to which you’re sweating.
punchline: In response, gamers asked, “What’s sweating?”

setup: A company has come out with a robot that makes salad.
punchline: So finally - a robot that’s not going to take away any American jobs!

setup: Long John Silvers has just hired a new executive to completely revamp their menu.
punchline: For starters, he said they're going to start experimenting with something called "fish."

setup: I like my coffee the way I like my jokes about the way I like my coffee.
punchline: I don’t drink coffee.

setup: In Florida, an Anheuser-Busch truck collided with a Frito-Lay truck, spilling beer and chips all over the highway.
punchline: Of course in Florida they call that an "Easter miracle."

setup: Starbucks just announced it will be raising its coffee prices.
punchline: When asked why, Starbucks said, "Because it’s been a week since we had any bad publicity. We had to do something."

setup: An 18-year-old has started a GoFundMe page so he can achieve his dream of taking a bath in KFC gravy.
punchline: So far, most of his donations have been provided by the Make a Sad Wish Foundation.

setup: "Game of Thrones" creator George R.R. Martin has put an end to the rumor that there will be a "Game of Thrones" movie.
punchline: Martin said, "There’s no way I could keep a character alive for two hours straight."

setup: A new study finds that men with thick biceps are more likely to live longer.
punchline: The study also found that I died 10 years ago.

setup: Over the weekend here in California, a riot broke out at a national surfing competition.
punchline: Nobody was killed, but one man is listed in stable but “gnarly” condition.

setup: In six states, bagged salads sold at Wal-Mart have been recalled.
punchline: The salad recall affects approximately 100 Wal-Mart stores and zero Wal-Mart customers.

setup: To celebrate Leap Day, Arby’s is offering a special vegetarian menu.
punchline: Arby’s said, "It’s part of our commitment to offer healthy food, once every four years."

setup: Over the last few months, Home Depot is reporting record profits.
punchline: Home Depot said they'd like to share the profits with their employees but even they can't find them.

setup: Dr. Dre may become the world’s first hip-hop billionaire.
punchline: So maybe my mom was right--I should’ve become a doctor.

setup: A company has created a bathroom scale that allows you to tweet your weight to your friends.
punchline: The company immediately went out of business.

setup: Uber has announced a new service where you carpool with strangers.
punchline: It’s a cutting edge new technology called, "taking the bus."

setup: Both the US and German teams have very good goalies, so many are predicting a very low scoring game.
punchline: So don’t expect to see one of those 1-0 blowouts.

setup: "Wind Beneath My Wings" is a great song, but what about the wind ABOVE her wings?
punchline: It’s technically just as important for lift.

setup: In LA this morning, a woman gave birth to a healthy baby on the shoulder of the 605 Freeway.
punchline: It's amazing what people will do out here just to use the carpool lane.

setup: Taco Bell is following up its Doritos tacos with new taco shells made of Fritos.
punchline: It’s all part of Taco Bell’s new slogan, "Working Our Way Down the Stuff You Find Next To a 7-Eleven Cash Register."

setup: In Germany, researchers were recently able to stop light from traveling for an extended period of time.
punchline: Here’s how they did it-- they placed the light on United Airlines.

setup: For its 25th anniversary, the music festival Lollapalooza is adding a fourth day.
punchline: That extra day will be devoted to showering.

setup: The pastor who incorrectly predicted the Rapture this Saturday was quoted as saying, "It's been a really tough weekend."
punchline: To make things worse, his friends keep calling to say, "Hey, come on, it's not the end of the world."

setup: This Valentine's Day, there's a new app called the "Love Calculator" that enables users to calculate their chances at love.
punchline: Of course sometimes the app goes by its original name, a "breathalyzer."

setup: This weekend "Spider-Man 2" earned $92 million at the box office.
punchline: That makes it the fourth most successful "Spider-Man 2."

setup: Apple recently said that every idea for an Apple product begins with "delight, surprise, love, and connection."
punchline: Apple said, "Then we add a $600 price tag on it and BOOM."

setup: A Southwest Airlines flight landed at the wrong airport in Missouri.
punchline: A spokesperson for Southwest said, "Close enough."

setup: Amazon Prime has made it possible to have beer and wine delivered to your home by Alexa.
punchline: All you have to do is say the phrase, "Alexa, Daddy’s sad."

setup: The very first Academy Awards ceremony lasted 15 minutes.
punchline: And thanks to the fast forward button on my DVR, so will this year’s.

setup: A new study says we should change how we feed cows so they don’t produce so much of the greenhouse gas: methane.
punchline: The first step they recommend -- eliminate "Taco Night."

setup: During the Super Bowl, Quicken Loans debuted a new app that lets people get a mortgage instantly on their phones by just tapping the screen.
punchline: The app is called, "What could possibly go wrong?"

setup: A Texas man has successfully fired the first-ever gun created by a 3-D printer.
punchline: Which raises the question – Don't you think a gun created by a printer would jam?

setup: Law & Order has released a 104 disc box set of every episode of the show.
punchline: Now fans of the Law & Order franchise have 2 options: either buy this exclusive 104 disc DVD collection or just turn on your television to any channel and wait 5 minutes.

setup: Facebook has announced a way for users to "unsend" messages.
punchline: All you do is go to the message center and click the button marked "I Was Drunk."

setup: New research shows that giraffes hum, but only at night.
punchline: Even more surprising: They all hum that Chili’s "Babyback Ribs" song.

setup: Pluto is larger than previously thought, and on its surface there is a shape that looks like a heart.
punchline: So now, scientists are deciding whether to classify Pluto as a planet or an emoji.

setup: Baskin Robbins introduced a new ice cream flavor called "Ice Cream Nachos."
punchline: They came up with the idea yesterday at 4:20.

setup: Just read a study claiming dogs can feel love, which is yet another way dogs are superior to cats.
punchline: And comedians.

setup: 7-Eleven announced it’s now offering "breakfast pizza."
punchline: It’s all in keeping with 7-Eleven’s motto: "If You’re Here, You’re Probably Hungover."

setup: An American judo fighter was expelled from the Olympics after testing positive for marijuana.
punchline: Officials became suspicious when he kept stopping the match and saying, "What are we fighting for, man?"

setup: A New York City pedicab driver is being investigated for charging Japenese tourists $720 for a 20 minute bike ride.
punchline: He’s been charged with impersonating a regular cab driver.

setup: I'm going to miss the World Cup when it's over.
punchline: It'll be hard to go into a bar & not hear people yelling about something I don't understand.

setup: Hey can someone send me an Oculus Rift VR headset?
punchline: I finally want to try parasailing.

setup: The Grateful Dead are putting out an 80-disc live box set.
punchline: No word yet on which Grateful Dead song it will be.

setup: I can't wait to try the new gigantic Starbucks size, "Trenta".
punchline: Or as it's called in The Midwest, "A Medium".

setup: A Spanish tennis player has been suspended after testing positive for meth.
punchline: Tennis officials grew suspicious when he started returning his own serves.

setup: The government has unveiled a new website that predicts your financial worth after graduating college.
punchline: It doesn’t give a number, it just tells you which Starbucks you’ll be working at and for how long.

setup: A man from Houston is attempting to visit all the Starbucks locations in the world.
punchline: It's been four years since he started and he still hasn't left Houston.

setup: According to new research, you may be at risk of bacterial infections from clothing you buy at the mall.
punchline: Experts say the store you most want to avoid is "Victoria's Really Disgusting Secret."

setup: The oldest person on Facebook is a 101-year-old woman.
punchline: She said, "I want to waste what little time I have left."

setup: A new study indicates 93% of women feel their armpits are unattractive.
punchline: The study was conducted by the Association of Researchers Who Have Run Out of Questions to Ask Women.

setup: The International Olympic Committee has officially recognized Ultimate Frisbee as an Olympic sport.
punchline: The news was greeted with excitement by thousands of guys named "Chad."

setup: The Garmin company is now offering a new GPS device that has the voice of Yoda.
punchline: Maybe it's just me, but if I'm getting turn-by-turn directions, do I really want someone who speaks backwards?

setup: The government shutdown will slash the budget for food inspection.
punchline: That’s bad news for health advocates, but great news for the new Japanese restaurant, "Leap-Of-Faith Sushi."

setup: A new survey has found that for the third year in a row, the most annoying word in the English language is "Whatever."
punchline: The news was taken especially hard by the top-secret government lab that developed "Brosephus."

setup: Earlier this week, investor Warren Buffett lost $2 billion.
punchline: Luckily, Buffett found it this morning under a pile of $8 billion.

setup: McDonald's has announced its Happy Meals will include an apple slice and half the amount of French Fries.
punchline: In a related story, the Happy Meal will now just be called, "The Meal."

setup: Campbells is recalling over 300,000 cans of Spaghettios.
punchline: Turns out, they contain a very dangerous substance called “Spaghettios.”

setup: It’s raining so hard now, we’re actually having mudslides here in LA.
punchline: This morning I was driving to work and I was passed by a house.

setup: A couple in Arkansas who love the Olive Garden have named their infant daughter "Olivia Garton."
punchline: Olivia went home today, where she joined her big brother, Hooters.

setup: A new study found that government employees are the happiest workers.
punchline: The study was conducted NOT at the DMV.

setup: Dartmouth College has named their medical school after Dr. Seuss.
punchline: Because nothing is better than hearing your doctor say, "You don't have cancer on your nose, you don't have cancer on your toes."

setup: Lufthansa Airlines will soon allow pet falcons aboard their flights.
punchline: This is bad news for Lufthansa passengers with seeing eye mice.

setup: Another day of heavy rain here in Los Angeles.
punchline: Which is great if you’re worried about the drought, or if you just like the smell of wet man bun.

setup: A former Target employee is accusing the store of hiring only attractive people as managers.
punchline: Apparently, he is talking about a Target I have never been to.

setup: A new study has found that beautiful people have totally different life experiences from the rest of you.
punchline: I’m sorry, I meant, the rest of us.

setup: A motorcycle gang in Canada is attacking businesses they don’t like by giving them mass one-star reviews online.
punchline: They're the fearsome badass biker gang known as "Yelp's Angels."

setup: A study has found that the air in Rome contains traces of cocaine.
punchline: So maybe Rome was built in a day.

setup: I’m on the Proterozoic Diet -
punchline: I only eat pre-chordates and metazoans.

setup: A new study just came out that shows that people who meet online are more likely to break up.
punchline: Later that night.

setup: Researchers are working on a breathalyzer that can tell if you’re driving while stoned.
punchline: Here's how it works - if the driver tries to dip the breathalyzer in nacho cheese, he’s stoned.

setup: Scientists believe they may have found a plant that is over a billion years old.
punchline: Turns out it’s the lettuce on a Carl’s Jr. burger.

setup: A German Olympic diver did one of the worst dives ever, and got a score of 0.0.
punchline: To try and save face, halfway through the dive, he yelled, "CANNONBALL!!!"

setup: A new survey found that Chipotle is one of the most popular locations to take a first date.
punchline: It’s also one of the most popular locations to break up if he’s still taking you to Chipotle after the fourth date.

setup: According to a new report, marijuana is the most popular drug on earth.
punchline: So better luck next year, bath salts that make you eat someone else's face.

setup: According to Time magazine, Cinco de Mayo is the 4th drunkest holiday in America.
punchline: The first three are St. Patrick's Day.

setup: I like to think of myself as the kind of boss who brings donuts in the morning.
punchline: Thinking about it is enough, right?

setup: According to the Washington Post, there is a national shortage of the hallucinogenic drug peyote.
punchline: But if you want to spend a week in the Mojave desert talking with coyotes, there's always Jagermeister.

setup: A woman in California is in trouble for injecting her 8-year-old daughter with Botox.
punchline: The 8-year-old is the first kid in history who made a face and it really did stay that way.

setup: A new study shows 88% of people disapprove of texting while walking.
punchline: The other 12% have been killed.

setup: A 102-year-old woman broke a pair of world track and field records.
punchline: The 102-year-old ran the 100-meter dash with a time of "February."

setup: I thought I’d seen it all, California.
punchline: Wow. Gluten-free urinal cakes?

setup: I’m what’s known as a "Tiger Dad."
punchline: If my kids don’t get straight A's, I threaten to practice the violin.

setup: A new study came out and it claims Washington, D.C. has the worst traffic in the country.
punchline: Government workers in D.C. spend hours in gridlock, getting nothing done and then, they get in their cars.

setup: According to a researcher at Harvard, success doesn’t lead to happiness, but happiness leads to success.
punchline: The researcher made the discovery after reading his grandmother’s throw pillow.

setup: An evangelical Christian rewrote "Harry Potter" so that all the witchcraft is removed.
punchline: And guess what - kids just love it! You can read the whole series - all seven "Harry Potter" books - in about 15 minutes.

setup: Scientists are testing out a new drone that would replace lifeguards.
punchline: Here’s how it works -- if you’re drowning, the drone would fly out and then drop a bomb on you.

setup: A man in Washington State is suing Monster Energy Drinks after he found a dead mouse at the bottom of his can.
punchline: In their defense, Monster Energy claims the can did say, "Now with a crunchy protein boost!"

setup: According to a new survey that just came out, Pizza Hut's new "Hot Dog Pizza" is the second worst pizza in America.
punchline: Which explains their new slogan, "Pizza Hut - Not The Worst Pizza in America."

setup: According to a new report, Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore is the best hospital in the country.
punchline: The worst hospital? Big Al’s Appendectomy Hut.

setup: I try to learn one new word a day and use it in a sentence.
punchline: Today that word was "today."

setup: The latest Rock Band videogame might be too realistic.
punchline: It’s just four smelly guys sleeping on a bus as they cross Ohio at night.

setup: A new study says that each prison inmate costs the city of New York the same as an Ivy League education.
punchline: Of course, it’s a ridiculous comparison, because inmates leave prison with actual job skills.

setup: My iPhone 6 Plus is two days old and it’s already bent.
punchline: Has anyone else had this issue after leaving their phone on train tracks overnight?

setup: A new study claims Oreos are as addictive as cocaine.
punchline: But the only difference is--when someone’s eating Oreos in a night club bathroom stall, it’s really sad.

setup: A man from Nepal set a new world record after kicking himself in the head 134 times in one minute.
punchline: He broke the previous record of zero.

setup: I finally got my tickets to the new Star Wars movie.
punchline: June 11 is a pretty good date, right?

setup: I'm a simple man.
punchline: I start every day with a cup of joe, the morning paper, and a lavender Pan-Asiatic body scrub from my man-servant, Lobo.

setup: A new report says that global warming could cause Boston to end up completely underwater.
punchline: Bostonians said, "We’re okay with that as long as happens when the Yankees are in town."

setup: According to new report, America’s teenagers are #30 in the world in math.
punchline: Luckily, American’s teenagers will never understand the report, because they’re 85th in reading. And #1 in Candy Crush.

setup: A new survey shows two-thirds of American adults pee in the ocean.
punchline: So good news -- maybe it’s not global warming that’s making the sea levels rise.

setup: A couple in England has paid thousands of dollars to get their dog a face-lift.
punchline: Apparently, the dog was so ugly, other dogs were sniffing his face.

setup: Researchers say much of Florida could be underwater by the end of the century.
punchline: On the bright side, they say it could happen much sooner.

setup: A new study finds drinking three pints of beer a week permanently dulls the brain.
punchline: So now you know: never stop at just three.

setup: A study reveals the best way to add years to your life is to exercise, lose weight, and not drink too much.
punchline: To which all of America replied, "What else you got?"

setup: According to a new survey, 50% of people believe robots will actually create more jobs in the long run.
punchline: When they heard this, robots said, "OH GOOD – THEY’RE BUYING IT."

setup: It’s Thursday, we’re pretty much one week away from Christmas.
punchline: So that means if you’re a guy, you have six days until you have to start shopping.

setup: I found a huge design flaw in my new iPhone.
punchline: People get angry when I talk on it during a funeral.

setup: A photo from Sochi has gone viral that shows an elevator with nothing but "up" buttons.
punchline: However, that is perfectly normal, says Sochi Olympics organizer Willy Wonka.

setup: Scientists are reportedly testing a new anti-aging drug that could lengthen the lives of dogs.
punchline: And even better -- shorten the lives of cats.

setup: A federal appeals court has said the NSA’s monitoring of Americans' landlines was illegal.
punchline: Now the NSA has to settle with the five people who still use a landline.

setup: A new study finds that the worst drivers drive a Prius.
punchline: Apparently, it’s very difficult to drive well while patting yourself on the back.

setup: I just heard someone logging onto AOL.
punchline: Instead of “You’ve Got Mail” the voice now says, “Greetings, Old Fool!”

setup: I hate it when adults try to relate to youth using slang.
punchline: Guess that’s what makes me a woke bae.

setup: A new study shows that germiest place in your kitchen is the refrigerator's vegetable drawer.
punchline: After hearing this, most Americans said, "We have a vegetable drawer?"

setup: My wife and I have an understanding.
punchline: When a gorgeous model comes on the show, my wife understands I'll do nothing.

setup: I’m having martial problems.
punchline: That’s not a typo, I have trouble conducting myself properly during wartime.

setup: In New York City, a woman gave birth in the back of an Uber.
punchline: Even more impressive: the Uber app told her, "The baby will be here in 5 minutes."

setup: A new company promises to give customers a pretend Facebook girlfriend for others to see.
punchline: It's yet another engineering triumph from the folks at "Sadtronics."

setup: According to Forbes magazine, the #3 highest paid actor in the world is Vin Diesel.
punchline: That works out to $10 million per "I am Groot."

setup: A New York woman is suing her surgeon claiming he was on his cell phone during her operation.
punchline: In response, the doctor said, "For your information, I was googling 'how to perform surgery.'"

setup: A Whole Foods store in New York will start offering customers cocktails while they shop.
punchline: It’s part of Whole Foods’ new slogan, "You’d have to be drunk to pay these prices."

setup: New research shows that dogs can distinguish a happy human voice from a sad one.
punchline: And yet they still can't distinguish a human leg from another dog's butt.

setup: In New York, a booze cruise ran aground near the Statue of Liberty.
punchline: If you think about it, that’s basically how my people came to America.

setup: New research finds that robots are just as bad as humans at assembling IKEA furniture.
punchline: In fact there’s a video that shows two robots trying to assemble the furniture, having a fight, then one says, "I knew it was too soon for us to move in together."

setup: An earthquake hit Las Vegas.
punchline: 1,200 Elvises were all shook up.

setup: New research reveals that being attractive in high school leads to success later in life.
punchline: The study also found that being nerdy looking in high school leads to a talk show later in life.

setup: Scientists have found a way to grow human tissue on apples.
punchline: Now the only thing left for them to discover is a reason to grow human tissue on apples.

setup: A new study says it costs $241,000 to raise a child to age 18.
punchline: However, that's mostly due to the candy cigarette tax.

setup: According to a new survey, forty percent of Americans approve of reading a partner's email if you suspect them of cheating.
punchline: The remaining 60% are cheating.

setup: According to a new dating survey, what men and women want most in a partner are good grammar and good teeth.
punchline: Which is why I never did well with my pick-up line, "I ain't don't never floss."

setup: An ex-Olive Garden employee has come forward to expose the truth behind the restaurant chain's Tuscany Italy Cooking School.
punchline: For starters: it's in Omaha.

setup: A group of researchers simulating life conditions for astronauts on Mars found that the most suitable foods are rice, Spam, and Nutella.
punchline: So apparently, I spent my freshman year of college on Mars.

setup: A new study came out and has found that reindeer populations are falling fast.

setup: A new study reveals Vermont businesses could benefit financially by legalizing marijuana.
punchline: And by Vermont businesses, I mean specifically Ben and Jerry’s.

setup: In New York City, a 106-year-old stockbroker is still at work on Wall Street.

setup: I can't decide which I prefer, burial or cremation.
punchline: Can you try one and then switch if you don't like it?

setup: A fragrance company has just come out with a cologne that smells like whiskey.
punchline: It's perfect for the guy who wants all the stigma of alcoholism but none of the fun.

setup: According to a new study, most men would like women to occasionally pick up the check.
punchline: The study also found that most women would occasionally like to be paid as much as men for doing the same job.

setup: A marijuana advocacy group is placing five pro-marijuana billboards around the stadium where the Super Bowl is being played.
punchline: Well, they were planning to, but then it just felt like so much work.

setup: According to a new survey, 75% of employees would rather get a cash bonus than spend time with coworkers at a holiday party.

setup: Researchers say that at least four species of crocodiles are able to climb trees.
punchline: Then, researchers said, "Sleep tight."

setup: According to a new survey, Facebook is the best company to work for in the upcoming year.

setup: A diner in North Carolina has taken all the prices off its menu, and has told customers to just pay "What God wants."

setup: A new trend is parents naming their kids after Instagram filters.
punchline: Frankly, I don’t see what the problem is - neither does my daughter, Sepia.

setup: A Wisconsin woman recently got a high school diploma at the age of 103, and said she is now considering going to college.
punchline: Friends are recommending a two-year college.

setup: A new report says America’s fast food restaurants are seeking alternatives to the term "fast food."
punchline: So far the leading choices are "fast-crafted" "fine casual" and "just trust us it’s meat."

setup: A new study found that nearly 1 out of 3 people can't resist using Facebook while in the bathroom.
punchline: I'm just grateful they're not using Skype.

setup: A sports medicine college has come out with its annual list of the fittest cities in America.
punchline: For the 4th year in a row, there aren’t any.

setup: A Japanese company bought the Jim Beam Whiskey distillery for 16 billion dollars.
punchline: Of course this morning, the Japanese company woke up in an alley and said, "I did what?"

setup: A new study says surgeons who play video games are better at their jobs.

setup: New research suggests that the first human beings drank alcohol millions of years ago.
punchline: The proof is a message from one caveman telling another, "I love you, Early Man!"

setup: I'm having a hard time calling the Sears Tower "Willis Tower"--it just feels wrong.

setup: A 17 year old boy sold an app to Yahoo for $30 million.
punchline: The boy says he'll use the money to fund his new website, "Who's A Nerd Now, Jenny?.com."

setup: In New York City, muggings for Apple products are up 40%.
punchline: Even worse, if you have the new iPhone, people camp out overnight to mug you.

setup: An anonymous bidder paid $1 million for a private lunch with billionaire investor Warren Buffett.

setup: A life-size statue of Ronald McDonald was stolen from a McDonald's in New Jersey.
punchline: Police are on the lookout for someone very sad.

setup: I’m going to go see the movie "Aloha."

setup: I like to teach my kids that they can do anything.
punchline: For example this year, our taxes.

setup: New research shows that William Shakespeare may have been a marijuana user.
punchline: I’m sorry, I find that absurd - Shakespeare wrote 37 plays, he was obviously a cocaine user.

setup: Scientists in Massachusetts have been able to grow a monkey arm in their lab.
punchline: Moments after being created, the monkey arm immediately threw poop at them.

setup: According to a new report, parents are naming their babies after characters from their favorite television shows.
punchline: I was shocked, and so was my son, "Cake Boss."

setup: A new report claims the US Postal Service could go out of business this winter.
punchline: On the bright side, the Post Office won't receive the report in the mail for another two years.

setup: Researchers are in the process of creating an underwater wi-fi network.
punchline: Finally, a way for people to tweet, "I'm drowning."

setup: A 13-year-old girl has become the world’s youngest psychologist.
punchline: Each session is an hour and she takes cash, checks or Instagram likes.

setup: According to a recent study, watching too much television on a daily basis increases your chance of a premature death.
punchline: The study goes on to say I'm worth it.

setup: According to a new survey, 42% of Americans have an unfavorable view of hipsters.
punchline: When they heard this, hipsters said, "Big deal – We had an unfavorable view of ourselves way before it was cool."

setup: A new report shows that due to the weak economy, more Americans are cancelling their cable television.
punchline: All I can say is, good luck trying to live without 8 shows about cakes.

setup: A new study says that, due to debt, 20somethings will retire 12 years later than their parents.
punchline: When they heard this, 20somethings said, "Retire from what?"

setup: A US astronaut has broken the record for the longest stretch of time spent by a human in space - 383 days.
punchline: The astronaut attributes this to determination, stamina, and "things being weird at home."

setup: A taxidermist in England said that for the past 30 years, he's only eaten road kill.
punchline: People are calling it the least popular Match.com profile ever.

setup: A man gave a waitress a $1,000 tip so she could take a trip to Italy.
punchline: It was an Olive Garden waitress whose dream is to one day try Italian food.

setup: My apologies to the nice people at the Lady Foot Locker in Sherman Oaks.
punchline: That’s all I can legally say for now.

setup: A new study just came out that found one part of Maine has the highest percentage of pot smokers in the U.S.
punchline: When they heard this, people in Los Angeles said, "Oh, it is on."

setup: A new app has come out that describes itself as "Uber for Sushi."
punchline: The app tells you exactly how many minutes away your E.coli is.

setup: Scientists say they are getting closer to developing a pill to replace exercising.
punchline: Americans heard this and said, "It better come in Cool Ranch flavor."

setup: A new study says that police DUI tests for marijuana are completely inaccurate.
punchline: Instead, it recommends that police just ask the driver, "Do you know how fast you were going - and WHAT DOES IT ALL MEAN, MAN?"

setup: A company in New Zealand has begun making a recreational jetpack that costs $100,000.
punchline: Experts are already calling it "The world's most expensive way to die."

setup: According to a recent survey, the most stolen vehicle in the U.S. is the Ford F-250.
punchline: And for the 10th year in a row, the least stolen vehicle is the Plymouth Anything.

setup: A brewer has come out with a beer that you can spread on toast.
punchline: It's said to appeal to a very specific market known as "alcoholics."

setup: Burger King announced that all of their chickens and pigs will now be raised cage-free.
punchline: In response, chickens and pigs said, "That's cool, now let's talk about the part where we get turned into sandwiches."

setup: NASA has announced plans for a much cheaper version of the Mars Rover.
punchline: In fact to cut costs, on the next Mars mission, the Rover will have a layover in Atlanta.

setup: In Australia, a woman fended off a crocodile by hitting it with her flip flops.
punchline: Authorities went to kill the crocodile, but it had already died from embarrassment.

setup: The CEO of Men’s Wearhouse was fired.
punchline: He’s filing a suit, an inexpensive, not very stylish suit.
